releases.name: Llama 4 Behemoth

announcement.title: The Llama 4 herd: The beginning of a new era of natively multimodal AI innovation
announcement.quote: We also trained a teacher model, Llama 4 Behemoth, that outperforms GPT-4.5, Claude Sonnet 3.7, and Gemini 2.0 Pro on STEM-focused benchmarks such as MATH-500 and GPQA Diamond.

sources.title: Meta delays "Behemoth" AI model release: report
Meta debuts the Muse Spark model in a 'ground-up overhaul' of its AI

releases.notes: Previewed April 5, 2025 (~288B active / ~2T total params, still training) as the teacher model for Llama 4 Scout/Maverick, with no numeric scores published by Meta. Repeatedly delayed through 2025 (reported mid-training MoE-routing and chunked-attention issues); Meta never issued a formal cancellation, but by April 2026 had moved its frontier effort to the closed-weight Muse Spark under Meta Superintelligence Labs and Behemoth was never publicly released. Recorded here as cancelled/abandoned rather than released.

releases.name: Llama 4 Maverick

announcement.title: The Llama 4 herd: The beginning of a new era of natively multimodal AI innovation
announcement.quote: We're introducing Llama 4 Scout and Llama 4 Maverick, the first open-weight natively multimodal models with unprecedented context length support and our first built using a mixture-of-experts (MoE) architecture.

scores.note: This is the base/pre-trained model's MMLU; the instruction-tuned model card reports MMLU-Pro instead of plain MMLU.

source.title: Llama 4 Model Card (Meta)
source.quote: Image Reasoning | MMMU | 0 | accuracy | No multimodal support | 69.4 | 73.4

releases.notes: Llama 4 Scout (17B active, 16 experts) launched the same day but is a smaller tier; Maverick (17B active, 128 experts) is the flagship of the initial Llama 4 launch. A larger teacher model, Llama 4 Behemoth, was previewed but not released (see meta-llama-4-behemoth).

releases.name: Muse Spark

announcement.title: Introducing Muse Spark: Scaling Towards Personal Superintelligence
announcement.quote: Today, we're excited to introduce Muse Spark, the first in the Muse family of models developed by Meta Superintelligence Labs. Muse Spark is a natively multimodal reasoning model with support for tool-use, visual chain of thought, and multi-agent orchestration.

sources.title: Introducing Muse Spark: Meta's Most Powerful Model Yet
Muse Spark Eval Methodology
sources.note: Describes how each benchmark (HLE, GPQA Diamond, ARC-AGI-2, SWE-Bench Verified/Pro, Terminal-Bench 2.0, LiveCodeBench Pro, tau-Bench Telecom, GDPval-AA) was run, but the document itself reports no actual scores/results table.

sources.title: Muse Spark Safety & Preparedness Report
sources.note: 160-page frontier-risk framework report (Chemical/Bio, Cyber, Loss of Control domains). Only non-standard variants appear (e.g. 'SWE-Bench Verified (hard subset)', 'Terminal-Bench Pro' 68.7%), none matching this project's tracked benchmark configs; no general GPQA/ARC-AGI-2/MMLU-Pro/AIME/SWE-bench Verified leaderboard table.

sources.title: Muse Spark 1.1 Evaluation Report
sources.note: July 9, 2026 update to the same Muse Spark checkpoint family; likewise structured as a safety/preparedness report with no general-capability leaderboard table. Reports 'resolved 24/42 unique tasks on SWE-Bench Verified Hard' (a dangerous-capability threshold metric, not this project's tracked pass@1 SWE-bench Verified config).

scores.note: Meta's launch post gives this single headline number for HLE via its extended "Contemplating mode"; no plain/no-tools HLE figure or other index-basket scores (MMLU-Pro, GPQA, SWE-bench, etc.) were published in the launch post or found in an official model card at time of writing. Re-checked 2026-09-07 against the Eval Methodology doc and the Safety & Preparedness Reports for Muse Spark 1.0 and 1.1 (see sources[]) — neither contains a general-capability comparison table with index-basket numbers.

source.title: Introducing Muse Spark: Scaling Towards Personal Superintelligence
source.quote: Contemplating mode provides significant capability improvements in challenging tasks, achieving 58% in Humanity's Last Exam and 38% in FrontierScience Research.

releases.notes: First model from Meta Superintelligence Labs (led by Alexandr Wang), closed-weight, available via meta.ai / Meta AI app with a private API preview. Point updates (Muse Spark 1.1, ~May 2026; reportedly 1.3 later) rolled the same model out further (voice, glasses, shopping) rather than establishing a new flagship generation, so they are treated as updates to this release rather than separate entries.
